questions.question: Which statement defines the critical edge-inference invariant?
options: Every device must activate a candidate as soon as its download starts
The current local model remains complete and callable until a replacement is verified and healthy
A cloud service must approve every individual inference
All hardware tiers must use one identical binary
questions.explanation: Atomic activation preserves a complete last-known-good artifact while an update is downloaded, authenticated, checked for compatibility, and evaluated.

questions.question: Why can a model that passes on a flagship phone still fail on an IoT camera?
options: IoT cameras always have faster accelerators
Quantization removes all operator differences
Memory, supported operators, accelerator speed, and thermal limits differ by hardware tier
Offline devices do not execute machine-learning models
questions.explanation: Deployment evidence is tier-specific because the compiled runtime, operator support, memory, latency, and power behavior depend on actual hardware.

questions.question: A 0.8MB delta is delivered once to 10M devices. What is the approximate transfer before retries and protocol overhead?
options: 800GB
8TB
80TB
340TB
questions.explanation: 0.8MB multiplied by 10 million devices is 8 million MB, or approximately 8TB using decimal units.

questions.question: What should happen when a downloaded model has an invalid publisher signature?
options: Activate it only on offline devices
Upload raw camera frames for manual inspection
Delete the current model before retrying
Reject it before activation and continue serving with the trusted current model
questions.explanation: Signature verification is an activation gate. A failed candidate must not replace the last-known-good artifact.

questions.question: A candidate causes an accuracy regression. How does a representative 1% canary change the outcome?
options: It can stop promotion after roughly 100K of 10M devices instead of exposing the whole fleet
It guarantees that no device observes the candidate
It removes the need for a rollback artifact
It makes slice-level quality evaluation unnecessary
questions.explanation: A staged cohort bounds the initial blast radius, provided its devices are representative and quality guardrails can pause promotion.

questions.question: Why is a retained rollback slot useful during an interrupted download?
options: It increases the model's benchmark accuracy
It keeps the complete current artifact available while the candidate occupies an inactive slot
It forces all inference into the cloud
It removes storage cost from the device
questions.explanation: Separate active and inactive slots let the runtime discard an incomplete candidate without corrupting the model that currently serves users.

questions.question: Which telemetry design best matches a privacy-first edge system?
options: Upload every raw sensor input for debugging
Disable all observability and drift detection
Send versioned aggregate health signals by default and use consented, time-bounded diagnostics for rare failures
Embed user identifiers in model weights
questions.explanation: Aggregate, versioned signals can measure fleet health with less exposure; exceptional diagnostics should be explicit and bounded rather than the default.
